transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-12
Time: 14:30 PST
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lin (Redwood AE), Priya Menon (Redwood SE), Michael Chen (CTO - Atlas), Sara Ortiz (ML Eng - Atlas), Liam O'Neill (Product - Atlas)
Links shared: deck: https://drive.google.com/atlas-redwood-deck , bench spreadsheet: https://app.redwood/benchmarks/atlas-70k (note: link auto-shortened)

Summary (auto): Discussed model candidates (Llama3 variants, Mistral, RedPajama, Falcon), requirements for 70k context, multilingual support (es/zh), and tool/function calling. Customer leaning Dedicated or Private for data residency but wants hosted POC first.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE on the account. With me is Priya, our SE. Michael, Sara, Liam, thanks for making time.
[00:12] Michael: Yeah thanks, Jordan. Quick agenda — we want to confirm which model families will work for our multi-ling chat assistant and if Redwood's hosted endpoints can handle our 70k context workflows, plus the security options.
[00:23] Priya: Cool. We'll cover model tradeoffs, expected latency/cost for high context runs, and deployment options (hosted, dedicated, private). We'll also note tool-calling/function support.
[00:35] Sara: To be upfront — we have a production timeline Jan next year. Primary musts: 70k context for long docs, Spanish and Mandarin support, function calling to external retrieval and DB, and SOC2/audit logs.
[00:47] Liam: Also, budget's tight — we care about unit token cost, but latency under 800ms per token for interactive flows is ideal.
[00:55] Jordan: Got it. High-level, folks generally look at hosted for fast POC, Dedicated for predictable throughput, and Private if you need VPC/on-prem with strict data controls. We'll run through model options.
[01:10] Priya: On models — the open-model ecosystem that plays well with Redwood includes Llama3 variants (2.7B, 13B, 70B), Mistral 7B/8x+ types, RedPajama-3, and Falcon 40B. For 70k context specifically we recommend models with long-context encoder optimizations — some Llama3 variants and RedPajama adaptors are good. Note: not all community checkpoints have 70k-token support out of the box.
[01:40] Michael: Wait, is there a big difference between Llama3 70B and a quantized Mistral for our use case? We care about cost.
[01:48] Priya: Yes. TL;DR: larger dense models give highest quality on complex reasoning, but cost and latency rise. Mistral-like families with quantization can hit a much lower cost per token but may exhibit regression on some longer-chain reasoning prompts. We can do hybrid routing — cheap model for retrieval/summary, larger model for final generation.
[02:10] Sara: How does Redwood handle KV cache for long contexts? We saw notes about "KV cache" in the docs but want more detail.
[02:18] Priya: We manage continuous KV caching and chunked attention for supported models. Quick caveat — some third-party checkpoints require adapter compilation; there may be extra prep time. Also sometimes the transcriptions in our internal notes say 'KV cash' ha, but it's KV cache.
[02:32] Liam: And function calling? We need tool-calling to our vector DB and ticketing system.
[02:38] Jordan: Redwood supports structured tool calling and function-like interfaces. We've got examples of retrieving and invoking retrieval embeddings, and returning structured JSON. There's a small difference between what OpenAI calls function calling and how an open model exposes a deterministic JSON structure — we add a validation layer.
[02:55] Michael: Data residency — EU and APAC users, can Hosted meet that?
[03:02] Jordan: Hosted can operate out of specific regions; for strict contracts customers often pick Dedicated or Private. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and predictable tenancy in chosen region. Private gives you customer-managed VPC and full control, but requires longer set-up and enterprise licensing.
[03:20] Sara: For encryption/KMS — do you support customer-managed keys and HSM?
[03:26] Priya: Yes on Private we integrate with customer KMS/HSM. On Dedicated we offer KMS integration and audit logs (we'll share SOC2 and ISO docs). Hosted supports encryption at rest and in transit but not customer HSM in the baseline plan.
[03:42] Michael: You mentioned compilation and kernel selection earlier. Does Redwood handle that automatically?
[03:47] Priya: Yup — our runtime will select optimized kernels depending on model and hardware. For new community weights we might run a brief compatibility pass and report perf profiles. That takes a day or two for a new checkpoint.
[04:02] Liam: Let's talk numbers — ballpark latency and cost for 70k context runs across Hosted vs Dedicated?
[04:09] Priya: Ballpark: for a 70k forward+KV read with a 13B long-context model on hosted, you should expect higher single-request latency (seconds) and higher per-run cost. On Dedicated with optimized kernels and batching we can drop latency and cost — maybe 30–50% improvement depending on batch and quantization. Exact numbers depend on model and quantization (int8/4). We'll run numbers on the benchmark spreadsheet.
[04:36] Michael: Can you do streaming for such long contexts? We want partial results to show to users.
[04:42] Jordan: Yes streaming is supported for generation tokens. For long context prep (embedding and retrieval) we can stream progressive summaries back while the full pass is ongoing.
[04:52] Sara: Multilingual quality — do we need separate models per language?
[04:57] Priya: Many of the recent models have multilingual pretraining but results vary. Llama3-70B tends to be stronger across languages, Mistral family is improving but some non-English edgecases exist. We can evaluate on your Spanish/Chinese test prompts during the POC.
[05:14] Michael: Any gotchas with tool-calling and long contexts? We've seen hallucinated function args in other stacks.
[05:22] Priya: Two mitigations: schema validation on the function layer and replay plus reranking. Also prefixing the function spec and example usage helps reduce hallucination. We often recommend a small verification step server-side before invoking external systems.
[05:38] Liam: Are there SLA differences between Hosted and Dedicated?
[05:41] Jordan: Hosted has standard uptime commitments, Dedicated comes with SLA-backed latency/uptime per contract and reserved capacity, which is why customers choosing Dedicated for production critical flows prefer it.
[05:50] Sara: For the POC we want Hosted initially to iterate quickly, but we might move to Dedicated for production. How fast can we move?
[05:58] Jordan: You can do a hosted POC in days. Moving to Dedicated typically takes a few weeks to provision capacity and set policies. Private/on-prem can take months depending on infra.
[06:10] Michael: Ok let's get into a practical config — we want to see Mistral-8x quantized and Llama3-13B long-context variants with 70k. Can you run both on Redwood and give perf and failure modes?
[06:22] Priya: Absolutely. We'll run them with your prompt set and share latency, token cost, and quality diffs. We'll also test hybrid routing (retriever->cheap model->final model) and provide a recommended routing policy.
[06:33] Sara: For experiments, do we need to upload data somewhere? We have sensitive docs.
[06:38] Jordan: For Hosted POC we can use a dedicated ingestion pipeline with limited retention and strict access, but if you need everything entirely controlled we recommend Dedicated with customer VPC peering or Private for fully air-gapped. We'll send our data handling doc.
[06:52] Michael: Any limitations around function calling — like number of tools, rate limits?
[06:57] Priya: There are rate limits on hosted tiers; Dedicated lets you raise those within your committed capacity. For tool-calling complexity it's more about designing robust schemas and validations; we can help design that during the POC.
[07:10] Liam: Let's talk quantization — int8 vs int4 tradeoffs and model compatibility.
[07:14] Priya: Some families compress well to int8 with minimal quality loss, int4 is more aggressive and may degrade complex reasoning. Our Optimize toolkit suggests quantization configs per workload; we'll run those recommendations for your prompts.
[07:28] Michael: Do you support custom fine-tuning or instruction tuning on top of open models?
[07:33] Priya: We support fine-tuning pipelines on Dedicated/Private deployments with proper governance. For Hosted we have managed fine-tuning with guardrails. We'll need to understand data sensitivity for fine-tuning.
[07:45] Sara: What's the typical cost to run a 70k token chain per request — even a rough estimate?
[07:51] Priya: Very rough: unquantized large models could be tens to hundreds of dollars per long-run. With quantization and dedicated capacity you can often reduce that substantially — sometimes by 3-10x depending on batching and cache reuse. We'll provide concrete numbers after running your sample prompts.
[08:08] Jordan: Quick interjection — we've noticed a lot of customers end up hybrid: use cheaper models for retrieval/condense, then call larger model for final step. That gives most of the quality for a fraction of cost.
[08:20] Michael: Sounds reasonable. On security checklist — SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs. Do you provide integrations?
[08:25] Priya: Yes SSO (SAML/OIDC), RBAC and detailed audit logs are available on Dedicated and Private. Hosted supports SSO too but certain enterprise features are Dedicated-only. We'll attach a feature matrix.
[08:39] Liam: Any known issues with RedPajama or community checkpoints?
[08:43] Priya: Community weights sometimes miss tokenizer or attention tweaks for very long contexts. We'll do a compatibility run and note required patches. And sometimes names get munged in notes — e.g., "Llama" as "Lama" in auto-transcripts.
[08:55] Sara: For the bench spreadsheet — can you include columns for tokens per second, tail latency (95/99), and cost per request?
[09:01] Jordan: Yes we'll include those. We'll also include multilingual accuracy metrics per language.
[09:08] Michael: How about local on-prem installs — what's involved for Private?
[09:14] Priya: Private is a heavier lift: customer infra prep, network peering, KMS, and an on-prem installer. Timeline is usually 2-3 months depending on readiness. We provide an SOW and runbook.
[09:27] Michael: Are there any prebuilt connectors for common vector DBs?
[09:31] Jordan: Yes — we have connectors for Pinecone, Milvus, Weaviate, and a generic S3/FS ingestion pipeline. We can add a custom connector for your in-house DB.
[09:40] Sara: For the POC, what telemetry will we get?
[09:44] Priya: Token-level cost, latency histograms, per-route dashboards, error traces, and prompt/eval diffs. We can give you a temporary console view for the POC.
[09:55] Liam: Any red flags on our end from what's described earlier?
[09:58] Priya: Only that 70k context pushes us to check model compatibility early. Also, multilingual edgecases — we'll need your test set. Otherwise timeline looks doable.
[10:09] Michael: Ok good. Let's set concrete next steps.
[10:13] Jordan: Recap — Redwood to: 1) run Mistral quantized + Llama3-13B long-context bench on your prompt set; 2) share SOC2/ISO and data handling docs; 3) provide pricing for Hosted/Dedicated/Private; 4) schedule perf deep-dive. Atlas to: share prompt set and note sensitive docs.
[10:30] Sara: We'll upload prompt set and a shortlist of failure cases by Monday.
[10:34] Michael: Also include a sample SLO definition for latency/cost that you'd recommend.
[10:38] Jordan: Will do. Priya, any final technical notes?
[10:41] Priya: We'll include quantization recommendations, expected improvements with batch/caching, and a draft routing policy (retriever->cheap->final). We'll flag any model checkpoints that need adapter work.
[10:52] Michael: Great. Thanks all.
[10:55] Jordan: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the materials and book the deep-dive for next week.

Auto-generated action items (end):
- Priya to run benchmark and publish spreadsheet link (see action items).
- Jordan to send pricing and compliance docs.
- Atlas to share prompt set and failure cases.

Notes about transcription: occasional name mislabels and small word confusions (e.g., 'KV cash' vs 'KV cache', 'Lama' vs 'Llama').

End of call.
